question_text: The woman ____ sold me those flowers spent twenty minutes wrapping them.
options: what
that
whose
explanation:
Đáp án B – that.
• Chỗ trống đứng ngay sau danh từ chỉ người "the woman" và đóng vai CHỦ NGỮ của động từ "sold" (người phụ nữ – đã bán hoa cho tôi). Đây là mệnh đề quan hệ xác định, dùng "who" hoặc "that". Trong 3 phương án chỉ có "that" → chọn B.
• A "what" sai: "what" không đứng sau danh từ để làm đại từ quan hệ (what = the thing which).
• C "whose" sai: "whose" chỉ sở hữu và luôn phải có danh từ đi ngay sau (whose + N, ví dụ: the woman whose shop…). Ở đây sau chỗ trống là động từ "sold" nên không dùng "whose".
👉 Mẹo: sau chỗ trống là ĐỘNG TỪ → who/that/which; sau chỗ trống là DANH TỪ → whose.

better
best
explanation: Có “than” nên cần dạng so sánh hơn. Với “well/good”, dạng so sánh hơn là “better”.

opened

question_text: You need ____ new shoes – those ones are too old!

buy

mustn't

question_text: If I were you, I ____ apologise.

would
can

question_text: We’re ____ in a beautiful holiday home at the moment.
options: stay
staying
stayed
explanation: “At the moment” cho thấy hành động đang diễn ra ở hiện tại. Với “we’re”, ta cần V-ing để tạo hiện tại tiếp diễn: “we’re staying”.

question_text: The letters ____ every morning.
options: deliver
are delivered
delivered
explanation: Chủ ngữ “the letters” là vật nhận hành động, nên dùng bị động. “Every morning” chỉ thói quen, nên dùng bị động hiện tại đơn: “are delivered”.

question_text: The cake tastes ____ delicious.
options: very
many
much
explanation: “Delicious” là tính từ, nên dùng trạng từ “very” để bổ nghĩa: very delicious. “Many” dùng với danh từ đếm được số nhiều, “much” thường dùng với danh từ không đếm được hoặc so sánh.

question_text: When I got home, Jenny ____ on the telephone.
options: was speaking
speaking
speak
explanation: Một hành động đang diễn ra trong quá khứ khi hành động khác xen vào. “When I got home” là hành động xen vào, còn Jenny đang nói điện thoại nên dùng “was speaking”.

question_text: He asked me if I ____ help him.
options: can
could
will
explanation: Đây là câu tường thuật. Khi chuyển từ lời nói trực tiếp sang gián tiếp, “can” thường lùi thành “could”: He asked me if I could help him.

question_text: The phone rang while I ____ dinner.
options: cooked
was cooking
cook
explanation: Một hành động đang diễn ra trong quá khứ thì hành động khác xen vào. “While I was cooking dinner” diễn tả việc tôi đang nấu ăn khi điện thoại reo.

question_text: When I was at school I used ____ a good student.
options: to be
be
being
explanation: Cấu trúc diễn tả trạng thái/thói quen trong quá khứ là “used to + V”. Vì vậy dùng “to be”.

question_text: I wish I ____ more free time.
options: have
had
will have
explanation: Câu ước về hiện tại dùng dạng quá khứ: “I wish + S + V quá khứ”. Vì vậy dùng “had”, nghĩa là ước hiện tại có nhiều thời gian rảnh hơn.

question_text: They had finished dinner before I ____.
options: arrive
arrived
had arrived
explanation: “Had finished” diễn tả hành động đã xong trước một hành động quá khứ khác. Hành động đến sau dùng quá khứ đơn: before I arrived.

question_text: It was ____ a nice day that we went swimming.
options: so
such
too
explanation: Cấu trúc đúng là “such + a/an + adjective + noun + that”: such a nice day that... “So” đi với tính từ/trạng từ, ví dụ “so nice that...”.

question_text: Coffee ____ to be much cheaper a few years ago.
options: would
has
used
explanation: “Used to be” diễn tả một trạng thái trong quá khứ nhưng hiện tại không còn như vậy. Câu nghĩa là cà phê trước đây từng rẻ hơn nhiều.

question_text: He denied ____ the window.
options: break
to break
breaking
explanation: Sau động từ “deny” dùng V-ing: deny doing something. Vì vậy câu đúng là “He denied breaking the window”.

question_text: I’ve got no plans for the weekend. Maybe ____ visit my parents.
options: I
I’m
I’ll
explanation: “Maybe I’ll...” diễn tả một dự định chưa chắc chắn hoặc quyết định có thể xảy ra trong tương lai.

question_text: The report ____ by the manager yesterday.
options: was checked
checked
is checking
explanation: Chủ ngữ “the report” nhận hành động kiểm tra, nên dùng bị động. Có “yesterday” nên dùng bị động quá khứ: “was checked”.

question_text: I'm thinking ____ moving to a bigger flat.
options: of
at
with
explanation: Cụm đúng là “think of + V-ing”, nghĩa là nghĩ đến việc làm gì. Vì vậy câu đúng là “I’m thinking of moving...”.

question_text: The museum ____ opened in 1998.
options: is
was
has
explanation: Câu có mốc quá khứ “in 1998” và nghĩa bị động: bảo tàng được mở cửa/khánh thành. Vì vậy dùng “was opened”.

question_text: I’m not sure about my future. ____ I will start a business.
options: Perhaps
Shall
Might
explanation: “Perhaps” là trạng từ nghĩa là có lẽ, hợp với ý không chắc chắn. “Might” nếu dùng thì phải là “I might start...”, không đi với “I will” như câu này.

question_text: There were only ____ people at the meeting.
options: a few
much
any
explanation: “People” là danh từ đếm được số nhiều, nên dùng “a few”. “Much” dùng cho danh từ không đếm được.

question_text: I’m reading a really ____ book on the history of Europe.
options: interest
interesting
interested
explanation: “Book” là vật gây hứng thú nên dùng tính từ “interesting”. “Interested” dùng cho người cảm thấy hứng thú.

question_text: A: Where is Lisa? B: She ____ be in her room; the light is on.
options: must
can't
needn't
explanation: Người nói suy luận chắc chắn Lisa ở trong phòng vì đèn đang bật. Dùng “must be” để diễn tả suy đoán chắc chắn.

question_text: They ate their lunch while they ____ coming home from school.
options: were
was
are
explanation: Chủ ngữ “they” đi với “were”. Cấu trúc quá khứ tiếp diễn “were coming” diễn tả hành động đang diễn ra trong quá khứ.

question_text: Neither Tom nor his friends ____ coming to the party.
options: is
are
be
explanation: Với “neither...nor...”, động từ thường chia theo chủ ngữ gần nhất. Chủ ngữ gần nhất là “his friends” số nhiều, nên dùng “are”.

question_text: I'm afraid I have ____ money left.
options: little
few
many
explanation: “Money” là danh từ không đếm được, nên dùng “little”. “Few” và “many” dùng với danh từ đếm được số nhiều.

question_text: If I ____ enough money, I would travel more.
options: have
had
will have
explanation: Đây là câu điều kiện loại 2, diễn tả giả định không có thật hoặc khó xảy ra ở hiện tại. Cấu trúc: If + S + V quá khứ, S + would + V. Vì vậy dùng “had”.

question_text: He’s about 40, but in this photograph he looks much ____ .
options: young
younger
youngest
explanation: “Much” thường dùng để nhấn mạnh so sánh hơn. Vì vậy cần “younger”: trông trẻ hơn nhiều.

question_text: The room ____ cleaned before the guests arrived.
options: had been
has been
is being
explanation: Việc căn phòng được dọn xảy ra trước một mốc quá khứ khác: “before the guests arrived”. Vì vậy dùng quá khứ hoàn thành bị động: “had been cleaned”.

question_text: She works ____ than her brother.
options: careful
more carefully
most carefully
explanation: “Works” cần trạng từ bổ nghĩa, và có “than” nên dùng so sánh hơn. Với trạng từ dài “carefully”, dạng đúng là “more carefully”.

question_text: She has ____ two books.
options: written
wrote
write
explanation: Sau “has” trong hiện tại hoàn thành cần quá khứ phân từ. Động từ “write” có V3 là “written”.

question_text: They decided ____ a new flat.
options: buy
buying
to buy
explanation: Sau “decide” dùng “to V”: decide to do something. Vì vậy câu đúng là “They decided to buy a new flat”.

question_text: She bought it herself, ____ she?
options: hasn’t
didn’t
shouldn’t
explanation: Đây là câu hỏi đuôi. Mệnh đề chính là quá khứ đơn khẳng định “She bought...”, nên đuôi phải là phủ định với “did”: “didn’t she?”.

question_text: I haven't seen him ____ Monday.
options: for
since
at
explanation: “Monday” là một mốc thời gian, nên dùng “since”. Câu nghĩa là tôi đã không gặp anh ấy từ thứ Hai.

question_text: She asked me where I ____.
options: live
lived
do live
explanation: Đây là câu tường thuật. Câu hỏi “Where do you live?” chuyển thành “where I lived”, dùng trật tự khẳng định và lùi thì.

question_text: I don’t recommend driving in the morning because there’s too ____ traffic.
options: much
many
most
explanation: “Traffic” là danh từ không đếm được, nên dùng “too much traffic”. “Many” dùng với danh từ đếm được số nhiều.

question_text: If the dress ____ been so expensive, she would have bought it.
options: hadn’t
weren’t
aren’t
explanation: Đây là câu điều kiện loại 3: If + had not + V3, would have + V3. Vì vậy dùng “hadn’t been”.

question_text: She is afraid ____ spiders.
options: about
of
with
explanation: Cụm tính từ đúng là “afraid of”, nghĩa là sợ điều gì. Vì vậy: She is afraid of spiders.

question_text: Do you know how long ____?
options: the film is
is the film
does the film
explanation: Đây là câu hỏi gián tiếp sau “Do you know”. Trong câu hỏi gián tiếp, dùng trật tự khẳng định: “how long the film is”, không đảo trợ động từ.

question_text: They asked us ____ late.
options: not to be
don't be
not be
explanation: Cấu trúc đúng là “ask someone not to do something”. Vì vậy: They asked us not to be late.

question_text: I never do my homework ____ I hate studying at home.
options: so
because
although
explanation: Vế sau đưa ra lý do cho việc không làm bài ở nhà, nên dùng “because”.

question_text: I'll let you know when I ____ the answer.
options: find
will find
found
explanation: Sau “when” trong mệnh đề chỉ thời gian nói về tương lai, ta dùng hiện tại đơn, không dùng “will”. Câu đúng: when I find the answer.

question_text: The restaurant ____ we had lunch was very cheap.
options: who
where
which
explanation: “Restaurant” là nơi chốn, và mệnh đề sau diễn tả nơi chúng tôi ăn trưa, nên dùng “where”.

question_text: I ____ a great book this morning – I really want to finish it.
options: was reading
read
have read
explanation: Người nói muốn nhấn mạnh việc đang đọc dở cuốn sách vào sáng nay và hiện vẫn muốn đọc tiếp để hoàn thành. Vì vậy “was reading” phù hợp hơn “read” hoặc “have read”, vì “have read” thường gợi ý đã đọc xong.

question_text: I'm used to ____ early every day.
options: get up
getting up
got up
explanation: “Be used to + V-ing” nghĩa là quen với việc gì. Vì vậy dùng “getting up”, không dùng động từ nguyên thể.

question_text: He promised ____ late again.
options: not being
not to be
don't be
explanation: Sau “promise” dùng “to V”. Dạng phủ định là “promise not to V”, nên câu đúng là “promised not to be late again”.

question_text: I'd rather ____ at home tonight.
options: stay
to stay
staying
explanation: Sau “would rather” dùng động từ nguyên thể không “to”: I’d rather stay. Nghĩa là tôi thích ở nhà hơn tối nay.

question_text: Excuse me? Can I try ____ this jacket to make sure it fits?
options: under
with
on
explanation: Cụm cố định khi mặc thử quần áo là “try on”. Vì vậy câu đúng là “Can I try on this jacket?”.

question_text: He didn't go to school ____ he was ill.
options: because
although
despite
explanation: Vế sau đưa ra lý do: anh ấy không đi học vì bị ốm. “Because” + mệnh đề là cấu trúc đúng. “Despite” đi với danh từ/cụm danh từ, không đi trực tiếp với mệnh đề như ở đây.

question_text: I wish I ____ speak French fluently.
options: can
could
will
explanation: Câu ước về hiện tại dùng dạng quá khứ. Với khả năng, “can” chuyển thành “could”: I wish I could speak French fluently.

question_text: They’re so different. I ____ , there’s no way they’ll be happy together.
options: mean
decide
wish
explanation: “I mean” là cụm giao tiếp dùng để giải thích/nhấn mạnh ý vừa nói. Ở đây người nói giải thích rằng họ quá khác nhau nên khó hạnh phúc.

question_text: It's the first time I ____ sushi.
options: try
tried
have tried
explanation: Với cấu trúc “It’s the first time...”, ta thường dùng hiện tại hoàn thành để nói về trải nghiệm đầu tiên: “I have tried”.

question_text: I saw Wi Joo this morning and she ____ if you were free tomorrow.
options: told
asked
said
explanation: Cấu trúc đúng là “ask if...” nghĩa là hỏi liệu có... “Told” thường đi với tân ngữ và “that”, còn “said” thường đi với “that”, không hợp trực tiếp với “if” ở đây.

question_text: They have lived here ____ they got married.
options: since
for
during
explanation: “They got married” là mốc bắt đầu trong quá khứ, nên dùng “since”. “For” dùng với khoảng thời gian, ví dụ “for ten years”.

question_text: Because of computers, many people don’t watch a lot of ____ now.
options: the television
a television
television
explanation: Khi nói chung về hoạt động xem TV, dùng “watch television” không cần mạo từ. “A television” là một cái TV, còn “the television” chỉ một TV cụ thể.

question_text: She can't come because she ____ her leg.
options: has broken
broke
was breaking
explanation: Việc gãy chân xảy ra trước đó nhưng kết quả còn ảnh hưởng hiện tại: cô ấy không thể đến. Vì vậy dùng hiện tại hoàn thành “has broken”.

question_text: There are two books here. Which one is ____?
options: your
yours
you
explanation: Sau động từ “is” cần đại từ sở hữu đứng độc lập: “yours” = của bạn. “Your” phải đi kèm danh từ, ví dụ “your book”.

question_text: He is interested ____ photography.
options: in
on
at
explanation: Cụm tính từ đúng là “interested in”, nghĩa là quan tâm/hứng thú với điều gì.

question_text: When I go to university, I may ____ history.
options: study
to study
studying
explanation: Sau động từ khuyết thiếu “may”, dùng động từ nguyên thể không “to”. Vì vậy: may study.

question_text: The test was easier ____ I expected.
options: as
than
from
explanation: Trong so sánh hơn, ta dùng “than”: easier than I expected = dễ hơn tôi mong đợi.

question_text: If it rains tomorrow, we ____ at home.
options: stay
stayed
will stay
explanation: Đây là câu điều kiện loại 1: If + hiện tại đơn, will + V. Mệnh đề kết quả dùng “will stay”.

question_text: This exercise is ____ than the last one.
options: difficult
more difficult
most difficult
explanation: Có “than” nên cần dạng so sánh hơn. Với tính từ dài “difficult”, ta dùng “more difficult”.

question_text: I think, in the future, people ____ live much longer than they do now.
options: ought
will
would
explanation: “In the future” và “I think” cho thấy đây là dự đoán tương lai. Dùng “will live”.

question_text: The more you practise, the ____ you become.
options: good
better
best
explanation: Cấu trúc so sánh kép là “The more..., the better...”. Nghĩa là càng luyện tập nhiều thì càng giỏi hơn.

question_text: It ____ be meat free – it tastes just like chicken!
options: could
can
can’t
explanation: Người nói suy luận món này không thể là đồ chay/không thịt vì nó có vị giống gà. Dùng “can’t be” để diễn tả suy đoán phủ định chắc chắn.

question_text: The man ____ lives next door is a doctor.
options: who
which
where
explanation: “The man” là người và đại từ quan hệ làm chủ ngữ của mệnh đề “lives next door”, nên dùng “who”.

question_text: They stopped ____ lunch at 1 p.m.
options: have
having
to have
explanation: “Stop to do something” nghĩa là dừng việc đang làm để làm việc khác. Ở đây họ dừng lại để ăn trưa, nên dùng “to have lunch”.

question_text: I met a man ____ brother works with you.
options: whose
who
which
explanation: Cần đại từ quan hệ chỉ sở hữu: anh trai/em trai của người đàn ông đó. Vì vậy dùng “whose”.

question_text: I'm not tall enough ____ the shelf.
options: reach
reaching
to reach
explanation: Cấu trúc “adjective + enough + to V” nghĩa là đủ... để làm gì. Câu đúng: tall enough to reach the shelf.

question_text: Call me tomorrow after 8.30, because I will just ____ at home.
options: about to relax
have relax
be relaxing
explanation: Người nói diễn tả hành động sẽ đang diễn ra vào thời điểm sau 8:30 ngày mai. Dùng tương lai tiếp diễn: “will be relaxing”.

question_text: The doctor says I will ____ much better by the end of the week.
options: to feel
be feeling
have felt
explanation: Câu nói về trạng thái/cảm giác dự kiến trong tương lai gần. “Will be feeling” là cách tự nhiên để nói sẽ cảm thấy khá hơn vào thời điểm đó.

question_text: I'm not used to ____ in big cities.
options: drive
driving
drove
explanation: Cấu trúc “be used to + V-ing/noun” nghĩa là quen với việc gì. Vì vậy: not used to driving.

question_text: I was made ____ the room after the party.
options: clean
to clean
cleaning
explanation: Ở dạng chủ động, “make someone do something” không dùng “to”. Nhưng khi chuyển sang bị động, cấu trúc là “be made to do something”. Vì vậy dùng “to clean”.

question_text: It was a dark, moonlit night when the traveller ____ at the inn.
options: arrived
was arriving
had arrived
explanation: Đây là sự kiện chính trong câu chuyện ở quá khứ: người lữ khách đến quán trọ. Sự kiện chính dùng quá khứ đơn “arrived”.

question_text: The film was ____ boring that I fell asleep.
options: such
so
too
explanation: Cấu trúc đúng là “so + adjective + that”: so boring that I fell asleep. “Such” cần danh từ phía sau, ví dụ “such a boring film”.

question_text: He used to ____ tennis every weekend.
options: play
playing
played
explanation: “Used to + V nguyên thể” diễn tả thói quen trong quá khứ. Vì vậy dùng “play”, không dùng “playing” hay “played”.

question_text: She doesn't like coffee, ____?
options: does she
doesn't she
is she
explanation: Câu hỏi đuôi: mệnh đề chính phủ định thì đuôi khẳng định. “Doesn’t like” dùng trợ động từ “does”, nên đuôi là “does she?”.

question_text: There's someone at the door, ____?
options: isn't there
is there
wasn't there
explanation: Câu hỏi đuôi với cấu trúc “There is...” ở dạng khẳng định sẽ dùng đuôi phủ định: “isn’t there?”.

question_text: I have my hair ____ every month.
options: cut
cutting
to cut
explanation: Cấu trúc nhờ ai làm gì là “have something + V3/ed”. Động từ “cut” có V3 vẫn là “cut”, nên câu đúng là “have my hair cut”.

question_text: ____ been reading this book now for a week and it isn’t getting any better!
options: I’ve
I’m
I’d
explanation: Cấu trúc hiện tại hoàn thành tiếp diễn là “have/has been + V-ing”. Vì vậy: I’ve been reading this book for a week.

question_text: If I hadn’t gone out last night, I ____ be so tired now.
options: won’t
wouldn’t
hadn’t
explanation: Đây là câu điều kiện hỗn hợp: điều kiện trái với quá khứ “If I hadn’t gone out last night” và kết quả trái với hiện tại “I wouldn’t be so tired now”.

question_text: The woman ____ you met yesterday is my aunt.
options: who
which
where
explanation: “The woman” là người, nên dùng đại từ quan hệ “who”. “Which” dùng cho vật/sự việc, còn “where” dùng cho nơi chốn.

question_text: The garden is looking untidy– you need to get rid ____ the weeds.
options: from
out
of
explanation: Cụm đúng là “get rid of”, nghĩa là loại bỏ. Câu đúng: get rid of the weeds.

question_text: This is ____ useful advice.
options: a
an
explanation: “Advice” là danh từ không đếm được, nên không dùng “a/an”. Dù có tính từ “useful”, ta vẫn nói “useful advice”.

question_text: We have ____ finished our homework.
options: yet
already
still
explanation: Trong câu khẳng định hiện tại hoàn thành, “already” diễn tả việc đã hoàn thành rồi. “Yet” thường dùng trong câu phủ định/nghi vấn.

question_text: He ____ be at home; his car isn't outside.
options: can't
must
should
explanation: Người nói suy luận rằng anh ấy không thể ở nhà vì xe không ở bên ngoài. Dùng “can’t be” để diễn tả suy đoán phủ định chắc chắn.

question_text: I ____ like mushrooms, but I can’t stop eating them now.
options: wouldn’t
didn’t use to
couldn’t
explanation: “Didn’t use to + V” diễn tả điều trước đây không xảy ra/không đúng nhưng hiện tại đã thay đổi. Câu nghĩa là trước đây tôi không thích nấm, nhưng bây giờ lại ăn nhiều.

question_text: We need to find out ____ caused the problem.
options: what
which
whose
explanation: Cần từ để chỉ “điều gì” gây ra vấn đề. “What caused the problem” là cụm mệnh đề danh từ đúng trong câu này.

question_text: We haven't finished the work ____.
options: already
yet
still
explanation: Trong câu phủ định hiện tại hoàn thành, “yet” thường đặt cuối câu để diễn tả “chưa”. Câu đúng: We haven’t finished the work yet.

question_text: I prefer tea ____ coffee.
options: than
from
to
explanation: Cụm so sánh sở thích đúng là “prefer A to B”. Vì vậy: I prefer tea to coffee.

question_text: The next meeting ____ on the sixth of June.
options: is holding
will be held
holds
explanation: Cuộc họp là thứ được tổ chức, nên cần bị động. Nói về tương lai, dùng “will be held”.

question_text: The newspaper China Today ____ published for over 60 years.
options: is being
has been
was being
explanation: “For over 60 years” diễn tả khoảng thời gian kéo dài từ quá khứ đến hiện tại. Chủ ngữ là tờ báo được xuất bản, nên dùng bị động hiện tại hoàn thành: “has been published”.

question_text: We arrived late ____ the traffic.
options: because
because of
although
explanation: Sau chỗ trống là cụm danh từ “the traffic”, nên dùng “because of”. Nếu dùng “because” thì cần một mệnh đề, ví dụ “because the traffic was bad”.

question_text: I don't mind ____ early.
options: start
to start
starting
explanation: Sau “mind” dùng V-ing: mind doing something. Câu đúng là “I don’t mind starting early”.

question_text: He made me ____ until midnight.
options: work
to work
working
explanation: Cấu trúc chủ động là “make someone + V nguyên thể không to”. Vì vậy dùng “work”: He made me work.

question_text: I don't know ____ to do next.
options: what
which
who
explanation: Cấu trúc “what to do” nghĩa là phải làm gì. “Which” dùng khi chọn giữa các lựa chọn cụ thể, còn “who” dùng cho người.

question_text: She said she ____ call me later.
options: would
will
is going
explanation: Trong câu tường thuật, “will” thường lùi thành “would”. Vì vậy: She said she would call me later.

question_text: ____ of China is very interesting.
options: history
A history
The history
explanation: Khi nói về lịch sử cụ thể của một quốc gia với cụm “of China”, cách tự nhiên là “The history of China”.

question_text: They said they ____ been studying for ages.
options: will have
are
had
explanation: Đây là câu tường thuật. Câu trực tiếp có thể là “We have been studying for ages”, khi tường thuật lùi thành “they had been studying for ages”.

question_text: If she had studied harder, she ____ passed the exam.
options: would have
will have
had
explanation: Đây là câu điều kiện loại 3: If + had + V3, would have + V3. Vì vậy dùng “would have passed”.

question_text: The teacher told us ____ carefully.
options: listening
listen
to listen
explanation: Cấu trúc đúng là “tell someone to do something”. Vì vậy: The teacher told us to listen carefully.

question_text: The train ____ at 7 p.m. tomorrow.
options: leaves
will leaving
is leave
explanation: Lịch trình cố định của phương tiện giao thông thường dùng hiện tại đơn, dù nói về tương lai. Vì vậy: The train leaves at 7 p.m. tomorrow.

question_text: My father, ____ is a dentist, told me not to drink sugary drinks.
options: who
which
that
explanation: Đây là mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định vì có dấu phẩy. Nói về người nên dùng “who”. “That” không dùng trong mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định có dấu phẩy.

question_text: The road was closed ____ an accident.
options: because
due to
although
explanation: Sau chỗ trống là cụm danh từ “an accident”, nên dùng “due to”. “Because” cần một mệnh đề đầy đủ, ví dụ “because there was an accident”.

question_text: You ____ have bought that car. What a waste of money!
options: shouldn’t
mustn’t
couldn’t
explanation: “Shouldn’t have + V3” diễn tả việc lẽ ra không nên làm trong quá khứ. Người nói cho rằng mua xe là lãng phí tiền.

question_text: She has been learning English ____ she was ten.
options: for
since
during
explanation: “Since” dùng với mốc thời gian bắt đầu. “She was ten” là mốc bắt đầu, nên dùng “since”.

question_text: By the time the police arrived, the thief ____.
options: left
had left
was leaving
explanation: Hành động tên trộm rời đi xảy ra trước khi cảnh sát đến. Khi một hành động xảy ra trước một mốc quá khứ, dùng quá khứ hoàn thành: “had left”.

question_text: He has ____ visited London twice.
options: yet
already
still
explanation: Trong câu khẳng định hiện tại hoàn thành, “already” diễn tả việc đã xảy ra. Câu đúng: He has already visited London twice.

question_text: I don't know anyone ____ can fix this computer.
options: which
who
where
explanation: “Anyone” chỉ người, nên dùng đại từ quan hệ “who”. “Which” dùng cho vật, “where” dùng cho nơi chốn.

question_text: The book, ____ I borrowed from Mai, is excellent.
options: who
which
where
explanation: “The book” là vật, và mệnh đề có dấu phẩy là mệnh đề quan hệ không xác định. Dùng “which”, không dùng “that” trong loại mệnh đề này.

question_text: This is a ____ train to London. It doesn’t stop on the way.
options: direction
directly
direct
explanation: Cần tính từ bổ nghĩa cho danh từ “train”. “Direct train” nghĩa là chuyến tàu đi thẳng, không dừng giữa đường.

question_text: ____ memory of the day I met the president is very special to me.
options: The
A
explanation: Ở đây nói đến một ký ức cụ thể, được xác định bởi cụm “of the day I met the president”. Vì vậy dùng mạo từ xác định “The”.

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Both pictures show people travelling, but in different ways. In the first picture, a couple is travelling by car. extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Both pictures show people in the middle of a journey, though the means of transport are different. In the first picture, a couple is driving along. The man, who has a beard and wears a blue denim shirt, is at the wheel, while the woman beside him, in a straw hat and a yellow top, is smiling happily. Both have their seatbelts on, and a child can be seen in the back seat, so this is probably a family trip. The second picture shows four passengers on a modern train, sitting in blue seats that face each other. They are chatting and holding cups, and one of the men is looking at his phone. An orange suitcase sits on the rack above them, and green countryside rushes past the window. Both journeys look pleasant, but the car offers privacy, whereas the train is a shared and more social space.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: The most recent present I got was a rather heavy one, a cast-iron frying pan. My younger sister gave it to me at the end of March, a few days before my birthday. She was flying back to Da Nang and could not wait for the actual day. She had noticed that every pan in my kitchen was scratched to death. So she decided to solve the problem herself, instead of buying me another scented candle I would never use. When it comes to presents in general, I lean towards handmade ones. A friend of mine once knitted me a scarf that was a bit crooked at one end, and I still keep it. Honestly, I cannot remember what I was given at my graduation. Handmade things carry the hours somebody spent on them, and that is hard to buy. That said, I would not be strict about it. If somebody needs a good pair of running shoes, a homemade card is not going to help them much. As for the near future, yes, I am planning something. My colleague Trang is leaving our office in September to study abroad. A few of us are putting together a photo album with short messages from everyone she has worked with. I am in charge of collecting the pictures, which means chasing about twenty people for old files. It is turning into far more work than I expected, but I think her reaction will make it worth the trouble.

extra_data.sampleAnswer: Passing the final accounting paper at university is probably the thing I am proudest of, even though it happened three years ago. I had failed the same exam the term before by two marks, which was humiliating, since most of my classmates had already graduated and moved on. So I set myself one clear goal for that term: pass, whatever it took. I worked through three or four past papers a week, gave up my part-time job in a coffee shop, and revised in the university library from seven in the morning because my flat was far too noisy. When the results came out I was on a bus, and I actually shouted. The other passengers did not appreciate it. My first feeling, oddly, was not joy but relief. extra_data.sampleAnswer: Last November I was asked to run a training session for new staff at my company. I was fairly nervous about it, because most of the audience were older than me. Afterwards my line manager Hoa stopped me in the corridor. She is not exactly generous with compliments, so I was surprised. She said my explanations were the clearest she had heard in years, and she wanted me to design the whole induction programme. It took me a moment to realise she was being serious. Honestly, it made my week. There was relief first, because I had spent three evenings preparing the slides. I genuinely thought I had rushed the second half. Then there was a kind of quiet pride that stayed with me for days. I remember walking home the long way just to enjoy it. What surprised me most was how much it changed my attitude at work. I started volunteering for things I would previously have avoided. That is exactly why I think positive feedback matters so much. People assume that others already know when they are doing well. In fact most of us are far more aware of our mistakes than our strengths. A few honest words can push somebody through a difficult period, and they cost nothing. Of course, praise has to be specific and deserved, otherwise it turns into empty flattery. Used properly, though, it is one of the cheapest and most powerful tools any manager has.

groups.question: Why do you think people find big changes difficult?

extra_data.sampleAnswer: I changed jobs in early 2023. I left a small logistics company where I had worked for four years, and joined a much larger firm in the same industry. The decision was not really about money. My old team had shrunk from twelve people to five, and there was nowhere left for me to grow. I handed in my notice in January and started the new position three weeks later. That sounds smooth, but it certainly did not feel smooth at the time. The first two months were a mess of mixed feelings. I felt relieved to escape a company that was clearly going downhill. I felt guilty about leaving colleagues who had become friends. I was also quietly terrified that I had overestimated myself. In the old office I knew every system and every shortcut. In the new one I had to ask where the printer was. It took about half a year before I stopped feeling like a visitor. Why are big changes so hard for people? I think we underestimate how much of our confidence comes from familiarity rather than ability. When everything around you is new, you lose all those small daily wins. Those wins quietly tell you that you are doing fine. There is also the fear of regret, because with any change there is a version of your life you gave up. Most of us prefer something imperfect that we understand.
extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: I changed my job in January 2023. Before that, I worked at a small logistics company for four years. The company was getting smaller every year. The team lost people, and there was no chance to grow. So I applied to a bigger company in the same field. I sent my application in December, and I started the new job three weeks after I left. The new company has about two hundred staff, and the office is also nearer to my home. I had many different feelings at the same time. I felt happy, because the new office was modern and busy. But I also felt sad, because my old colleagues were my friends. In the first month I was nervous every morning. I did not know the systems, and I asked many simple questions. One kind colleague helped me with everything. After about six months I finally felt comfortable there. Why is change so hard for people? I think we love the things that we know well. When everything is new, we feel weak and slow. People are also afraid of making the wrong choice. For example, my brother stayed in a bad job for years, because he was simply afraid of a new start. But in my case, the change was worth it.

question_text: What are the benefits of markets and supermarkets?
explanation: Markets and supermarkets both have many benefits. Markets often sell fresh food, such as vegetables, fruit, meat, and local products. They also have a friendly atmosphere, and customers can sometimes bargain for better prices. Supermarkets are convenient because they offer many products in one place, from food to household items. They are usually clean, organized, and open for longer hours. Both places help people buy what they need every day.

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Markets and supermarkets both have many benefits. Markets often sell fresh food, such as vegetables, fruit, meat, and local products. They also have a friendly atmosphere, and customers can sometimes bargain for better prices. Supermarkets are convenient because they offer many products in one place, from food to household items. They are usually clean, organized, and open for longer hours. Both places help people buy what they need every day.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: They serve different needs. At my local market the vegetables were picked that morning, and prices drop after four o'clock. The woman who sells me herbs always adds extra without being asked. Supermarkets can't compete on freshness, but they win on everything else: fixed prices, air conditioning, late opening, and a card machine. My mother still buys food at the market and uses the supermarket for washing powder. Each place covers what the other cannot. I use both in the same week, and that balance works well.

explanation: Most people learn cooking from family - parents or grandparents are the first teachers. They pass down traditional recipes, and it's usually a mix of watching, helping out, and eventually doing it yourself. Some learn by trial and error, experimenting with food at home. question_text: Why is it important for people to learn how to cook for themselves?
explanation: Knowing how to cook is such a key life skill. It helps you eat healthier, save money, and control what goes into your meals. Cooking gives you independence - you don't have to rely on takeout or someone else to feed you. Plus, it's creative and satisfying to make something with your own hands. It's also great for connecting with others; cooking for family or friends can be a way to bond and show love. Being able to whip up a tasty meal feels pretty awesome!

question_text: Why do some people not like going shopping?
explanation: Many people do not like going shopping because it can be tiring and time-consuming. In busy shops or supermarkets, people may have to wait in long lines and walk around for a long time. Crowded places can also be noisy and stressful. Some people do not enjoy choosing between too many products, while others dislike spending money. That is why many people prefer shopping online because it is quicker and easier.

extra_data.sampleAnswerBasic: Many people do not like going shopping because it can be tiring and time-consuming. In busy shops or supermarkets, people may have to wait in long lines and walk around for a long time. Crowded places can also be noisy and stressful. Some people do not enjoy choosing between too many products, while others dislike spending money. That is why many people prefer shopping online because it is quicker and easier.
extra_data.sampleAnswerAdvanced: Shopping eats time, and that's the real complaint. You queue, you carry, you park, and after an hour you've bought three things you never planned to buy. Crowded centres at the weekend are loud and hot, which puts a lot of people off completely. There's also the tiring business of choosing between twenty similar products. That's why apps have taken over: my brother hasn't entered a shop in months, and he's proud of it. Shopping stopped being a day out years ago. Convenience won quietly.

people.text: Before trying any extreme sport, I believe it’s absolutely essential to train properly. That’s why I always make sure to take a training course and understand the safety rules before I try anything new. With the right preparation, I think extreme sports can be a great experience.

people.name: B
people.text: What I love most about extreme sports is how they let me enjoy nature in a different way. Activities like rock climbing or mountain biking allow me to explore amazing places while challenging myself physically and mentally. It’s a way to disconnect from daily life and feel completely alive. If I had more time and money, I’d love to do these kinds of sports more often, especially in wild, remote areas.

people.name: C
people.text: I’ve always been more into traditional sports like swimming, running, or playing tennis. They’re fun and easy to do regularly. But a few months ago, I went bungee jumping during a holiday, and it was an incredible experience. I didn’t expect to enjoy it so much! I still prefer regular sports for everyday fitness, but now I’m definitely more open to trying extreme sports once in a while for the adventure

people.name: D
people.text: I know some people find extreme sports exciting, but for me, they’ve never been important. I actually avoid them as much as possible. I don’t like the idea of putting myself in danger just for fun. There are plenty of safer ways to stay active and enjoy life. I’d rather go for a walk or do yoga than jump out of a plane or climb a mountain. It’s just not my thing.

people.name: Odilia
people.text: When I was a child, I would spend hours playing board games. The rules were straightforward and easy to understand. people.name: Chris
people.text: I was very lucky to grow up in a place with good weather. I loved going outside to play with my peers. We just chased each other around. question_text: The Arrival of the Four-Day Work Week
options: A way of life now out of date
Benefits for employees
Undesirable financial consequences
Unforeseen challenges for employees
Difficult to change old habits
An unfair plan for some people
Alternative solutions worth considering
Businesses preparing for a new policy
explanation:
--- GIẢI THÍCH ---
1. "A way of life now out of date" → Henry Ford cắt từ 48 xuống 40 giờ tạo ra tuần 5 ngày, nhưng "what once looked progressive is no longer the norm for 21st-century workers" — nếp cũ đã lỗi thời.
2. "Benefits for employees" → cả đoạn là lợi ích cho nhân viên: "higher job satisfaction, lower stress", "balance work with personal life", chia sẻ việc chăm con.
3. "Undesirable financial consequences" → toàn số liệu tiền bạc của doanh nghiệp: "output falling by as much as 20%", "sharp rise in running costs", "pushes up spending on wages, training and supervision".
4. "Unforeseen challenges for employees" → những cái KHÔNG NGỜ xảy ra với chính người lao động: tưởng vui hơn nhưng "satisfaction settles back to where it started" (hedonic treadmill), rồi "working faster is how accidents happen", "more strained than they were on the old schedule". Không chọn "An unfair plan" vì đoạn này không so sánh nhóm nào được lợi hơn nhóm nào.
5. "Difficult to change old habits" → dù được nghỉ, người ta vẫn quay về nếp cũ: "some employees drifted back to the factory floor of their own accord", "others picked up a second job to fill the hours". Không chọn "Undesirable financial consequences" vì heading đó đã dùng cho đoạn 3 và đoạn 3 nói về tiền của doanh nghiệp, còn đây là thói quen của cá nhân.
6. "An unfair plan for some people" → nhân viên văn phòng được lợi còn "teachers gain nothing", bác sĩ y tá "how can doctors and nurses work any less?", lính cứu hoả vẫn phải trực; câu chốt "widening the gap between one kind of work and another" = bất công. Không chọn "Unforeseen challenges" vì đoạn này không nói về hậu quả bất ngờ, mà nói về ai được ai không.
7. "Alternative solutions worth considering" → đoạn liệt kê 3 cách khác thay cho tuần 4 ngày: "Raising basic pay", "Improving social welfare", "Adding more public holidays".
Nhiễu: "Businesses preparing for a new policy" — không đoạn nào nói doanh nghiệp đang chuẩn bị áp dụng chính sách; đoạn 3 chỉ nói doanh nghiệp bị tốn tiền.
👉 Mẹo: heading có "unfair" → tìm đoạn so sánh nhóm này được / nhóm kia không (đoạn 6). Heading có "challenges" → tìm đoạn nói hậu quả xấu xảy ra với chính người áp dụng (đoạn 4). Heading "old habits" → tìm hành động quay về cách cũ (đoạn 5).

extra_data.title: The Arrival of the Four-Day Work Week

headings.text: An unfair plan for some people
A way of life now out of date
Businesses preparing for a new policy

paragraphs.text: Proponents of the four-day workweek argue that shortening the working week is both realistic and overdue. History, they say, is on their side. During the era of industrialization, the car magnate Henry Ford cut his factories' schedule from 48 hours down to 40, without touching wages - a move that helped establish the five-day pattern still followed in most workplaces today. Yet what once looked progressive is no longer the norm for 21st-century workers. As technology and science advance, a growing number of jobs no longer require workers to be physically present in the office five days a week.

The clearest gains, advocates say, are felt by employees themselves. Workers report higher job satisfaction, lower stress and stronger motivation to contribute. An extra day off makes it easier to balance work with personal life, leaving room to care for family, rest properly or take up interests outside the office. Advocates also point to a wider effect at home: with an extra day free, employees can share the childcare that in many households falls almost entirely on their wives, who often have to give up employment and the chance to pursue a profession of their own. Others are unconvinced, arguing that child-care facilities can already handle this perfectly well.

The financial side is where doubts surface most quickly. When Japanese firms began trimming their schedules in the late 1980s, following a nationwide push to bring working hours down, some reported output falling by as much as 20% over the first year, along with a sharp rise in running costs. Companies in retail and hospitality face a particular difficulty, since their doors have to stay open whether or not staff numbers are cut. Covering those hours usually means taking on extra people, which pushes up spending on wages, training and supervision. For a small firm, these extra costs alone can be enough to rule the idea out.

Supporters argue that shorter hours simply make people happier. Others call that claim unfounded, pointing to the hedonic treadmill - the tendency for satisfaction to settle back to where it started, so that within months workers drift back to their usual level of contentment no matter how long or short their week has become. Worse, a shorter week may not even deliver the relief people expect. One French company recorded a rise in productivity after cutting its hours, though sceptics suspect the gain did not last. Fewer hours means working faster, and working faster is how accidents happen. Rushing through the same volume of tasks in less time can prove deeply stress-inducing, leaving employees more strained than they were on the old schedule.

There is the question of income. Fewer hours on the clock can mean a smaller income, and for workers on modest wages that difference matters. Others find the empty day harder to fill than they imagined, and boredom sets in when there is little to occupy them. Where shorter weeks have been tried on a national scale, the results have been telling: some employees drifted back to the factory floor of their own accord, while others picked up a second job to fill the hours they had just been given.

Not every job can bend that way. Office staff may do well out of a shorter week, but many roles simply cannot work like that. Schools stay open on the same timetable and students still have to be taught, so teachers gain nothing. Hospitals take in the same number of patients whether the week is four days or five, so how can doctors and nurses work any less? Fires still break out and emergencies still happen, and firefighters have to be there when they do. Crime rates do not fall just because the working week is shorter. Critics warn that a change like this would help those who are already comfortable and leave everyone else where they are, widening the gap between one kind of work and another.

Many people remain convinced that the case for cutting working hours is unfounded, and point instead to other ways of reaching the same goal. Raising basic pay would leave workers better off without touching the timetable at all. Improving social welfare - better healthcare, childcare and pensions - would ease the pressure on households more directly than an extra day at home. Adding more public holidays to the national calendar would give everyone extra rest without asking a single business to restructure the way it operates. Each of these, supporters argue, delivers what a shorter week promises while avoiding the problems it creates.

▸ Family sports day — thứ tự đúng:
  0. "Last weekend the weather was good, so the town held a family sports day in the park." → câu cho sẵn, giới thiệu sự kiện.
  1. "It started early on Saturday morning with a ten-mile race for adults." → "It" trỏ về "a family sports day".
  2. "Sixty men and women ran in this, and Ms Kamur won with a very fast time." → "ran in this" trỏ về "a ten-mile race".
  3. "After she had received her prize, the children's activities and competitions began." → "she" trỏ về Ms Kamur ở câu trước.
  4. "These included football, swimming and jumping, and the children had lots of fun." → "These" trỏ về "the children's activities and competitions".

▸ Making films — thứ tự đúng:
  0. "In 1895, the Grand Café in France showed the first ever commercial film." → câu cho sẵn, nêu mốc thời gian và sự kiện đầu tiên.
  1. "Films from that period were very different from films of today." → "that period" trỏ thẳng về năm 1895 ở câu cho sẵn.

extra_data.title: Early Australia

headings.text: Technology helps uncover the ocean's secret
A new evidence that leads to speculation
Determination of the explorers through the ages

paragraphs.text: Some researchers are rethinking the traditional narrative of how Australia was settled. While it is widely believed that the first people arrived via land bridges from Southeast Asia during the Ice Age, new theories suggest otherwise. Alternative histories propose that early humans may have used rudimentary boats to cross from distant shores far earlier than previously estimated. These claims are controversial but are supported by some archaeological findings and oral traditions of Indigenous communities. Such ideas challenge the Eurocentric view of exploration and emphasize the ingenuity of early seafarers long before written records existed.

The vast Australian outback and its harsh deserts have long posed a formidable challenge to resettlement and development. For thousands of years, the central areas of the continent were difficult to inhabit due to extreme heat, scarce water sources, and isolation. Even after European arrival, these natural barriers prevented deeper exploration and settlement for decades. Today, the environment still remains an obstacle, limiting infrastructure, agriculture, and population growth in these regions. The Australian landscape, while beautiful and iconic, continues to shape the way communities are formed and connected.

Advancements in marine technology have revolutionized our understanding of ancient migration routes to Australia. Underwater sonar mapping and satellite imaging have revealed submerged land masses and potential seafaring paths once used by early humans. Archaeologists are now uncovering tools and fossils deep beneath coastal waters, which provide new insights into how long ago people arrived on the continent. These discoveries would not be possible without modern equipment that allows exploration of areas previously inaccessible. As research continues, scientists hope to fill in many historical gaps that have puzzled historians for centuries.

It is now widely believed that the journey to Australia wasn't completed in one go. Instead, early humans likely reached the continent in stages, moving through island chains and coastal areas over generations. This theory is supported by the distribution of artifacts and remains across Southeast Asia and Northern Australia. The idea of gradual migration, rather than a single wave, helps explain the diversity of early populations found on the continent. This step-by-step approach also reflects how ancient peoples adapted to different environments as they moved closer to the Australian mainland.

In recent years, new evidence has emerged from both land and sea, prompting scientists to re-evaluate earlier assumptions. A set of ancient tools discovered in a Northern Territory cave doesn't match previously known Aboriginal designs, leading some to speculate about earlier migrations or even contact with other civilizations. Additionally, genetic studies hint at complex interactions with now-extinct human species. These findings, while not yet definitive, open the door to exciting discussions and possibilities about Australia's earliest human history.

Many of the first explorers to attempt crossing Australia's interior were ill-prepared for the harsh conditions they encountered. Without sufficient knowledge of the land or survival skills in such a hostile environment, numerous expeditions ended in tragedy. The lack of understanding of the Aboriginal methods of finding water, navigating terrain, and managing heat led to avoidable suffering. It wasn't until later that European settlers began to adapt, learning from Indigenous Australians how to travel and survive in such an unfamiliar landscape.

Despite the many difficulties, both ancient and modern explorers showed incredible perseverance in reaching and understanding Australia. Whether navigating unknown seas in simple rafts or trekking across searing deserts with limited supplies, their determination pushed the boundaries of what was thought possible. Stories of survival and discovery continue to inspire awe, reminding us of the strength and courage required to explore the unknown. Through the centuries, this spirit of exploration has become a core part of Australian history and identity.

extra_data.title: Women Mathematicians.

headings.text: Attempting to create a gender balance
Labels can change perspective on people
A long career showing exceptional ability

paragraphs.text: For centuries, the achievements of women in mathematics were either omitted from historical records or attributed to male colleagues. Hypatia of Alexandria, one of the earliest known female mathematicians, was respected in her time, yet many of her contributions were later credited to male scholars. Such erasure has been a recurring theme in the history of women in this field.

Emmy Noether, often described as the most important woman in the history of mathematics, revolutionized abstract algebra and theoretical physics. Albert Einstein referred to her work as "the very expression of the spirit of modern algebra." Only recently has her legacy gained the widespread recognition it deserves, demonstrating a growing effort to acknowledge those once overlooked.

In many historical accounts, the success of male mathematicians has overshadowed the collaborative efforts of their female peers. For example, the development of chaos theory often credits Edward Lorenz, yet contributions by female mathematicians working in the same field are frequently omitted from textbooks and academic narratives.

Mary Cartwright had a mathematical career spanning over six decades. Her work in nonlinear differential equations laid the groundwork for chaos theory, influencing both mathematics and engineering. Despite the challenges faced by women in academia during her time, she maintained a consistent output of high-quality research throughout her life.

When female mathematicians are described as "women geniuses" or "female prodigies," the gender label, while well-intended, often implies that excellence is rare among women. Such terms, though celebratory, can unintentionally reinforce the idea that women's success in mathematics is unusual, rather than simply the result of talent and hard work.

To address the gender imbalance in mathematics, many universities and organizations now run outreach programs, offer scholarships specifically for women, and encourage female mentorship in STEM fields. These efforts aim not to give unfair advantage, but to create equal opportunities in a domain where women have historically been underrepresented.

In efforts to level the playing field, some institutions have implemented standardized criteria for admissions or research evaluation. However, such uniform methods can sometimes ignore the diverse paths and challenges faced by individuals, particularly women balancing academic and societal expectations. A one-size-fits-all approach may not always foster true equity.

question_text: Put the sentences in the correct order.
options: Even though it was crowded, the staff still managed to find a table for me.
It tasted really good with melted cheese on top, and I’ll definitely come back to this place again.
After checking them all, I decided to order the most expensive sandwich.
They handed me the menu, and when I looked through it, I saw quite a variety of dishes.
When I arrived, the place was very crowded, and the staff were extremely busy on the first day.
In the evening, she relaxes by reading books on productivity and well-being.
At lunchtime, she enjoys a homemade sandwich prepared with fresh ingredients.
The company offers flexible working hours to better support employees’ schedules.
One employee uses a planner to organize her tasks throughout her flexible workweek.
Every morning, she works at a white desk in the shared open office.
explanation:
--- GIẢI THÍCH ---
Dạng sắp xếp câu: tìm câu mở đầu (không trỏ ngược), rồi bám vào đại từ, từ chỉ định và từ nối để nối dần.

▸ My visit to a new coffee shop — thứ tự đúng:
  1. “When I arrived, the place was very crowded, and the staff were extremely busy on the first day.” → câu mở đầu, nêu bối cảnh.
  2. “Even though it was crowded, the staff still managed to find a table for me.” → “it was crowded” nối tiếp ý đông khách.
  3. “They handed me the menu, and when I looked through it, I saw quite a variety of dishes.” → “They” = the staff.
  4. “After checking them all, I decided to order the most expensive sandwich.” → “them all” = a variety of dishes.
  5. “It tasted really good with melted cheese on top, and I’ll definitely come back to this place again.” → “It” = the sandwich; câu kết.

▸ Flexible working — thứ tự đúng:
  1. “The company offers flexible working hours to better support employees’ schedules.” → câu mở đầu: nêu chủ thể và bối cảnh, không trỏ ngược về câu nào.
  2. “One employee uses a planner to organize her tasks throughout her flexible workweek.” → nối tiếp mạch nội dung của câu ngay trước.
  3. “Every morning, she works at a white desk in the shared open office.” → nối tiếp mạch nội dung của câu ngay trước.
  4. “At lunchtime, she enjoys a homemade sandwich prepared with fresh ingredients.” → nối tiếp mạch nội dung của câu ngay trước.
  5. “In the evening, she relaxes by reading books on productivity and well-being.” → nối tiếp mạch nội dung của câu ngay trước.

options: In these performances, he liked to wear bright clothes and paint his face.
This strange way of dressing and his songs have attracted people's attention.

This helped him receive many invitations for collaborations and performances.

explanation:
--- GIẢI THÍCH ---
Dạng sắp xếp câu: tìm câu mở đầu (không trỏ ngược), rồi bám vào đại từ, từ chỉ định và từ nối để nối dần.

▸ A famous singer — thứ tự đúng:
  0. "Jade Nobelton is only 18 years old, and he is a famous singer." → câu cho sẵn, giới thiệu nhân vật.
  1. "Before becoming famous at this young age, he studied art and music at high school." → "this young age" trỏ về "18 years old".
  2. "During this education, he learned to be creative and to practise singing on stage." → "this education" trỏ về việc học ở high school.
  3. "In these performances, he liked to wear bright clothes and paint his face." → "these performances" trỏ về "singing on stage".
  4. "This strange way of dressing and his songs have attracted people's attention." → "This strange way of dressing" trỏ về quần áo sặc sỡ và vẽ mặt.
  5. "They started to follow him on social media, and now he is very popular." → "They" trỏ về "people" ở câu trước, chốt bằng kết quả hiện tại.

▸ Music show at the park — thứ tự đúng:
  0. "Last Saturday there was a music show in the park." → câu cho sẵn.
  1. "The local authorities planned, sponsored and paid for everything." → "everything" chỉ toàn bộ buổi diễn ở câu cho sẵn; chính quyền tài trợ hết.
  2. "Because it was free, nearly 5,000 people attended." → "Because it was free" là hệ quả của việc chính quyền trả tiền.
  3. "They came early and sat in nearby shops where they could see the performances." → "They" là 5.000 người vừa nhắc; họ đến sớm và ngồi trong các cửa hàng gần đó.
  4. "Although the staff had a busy day, they closed the shops early to watch the singer perform." → "the staff" là nhân viên của các cửa hàng ở câu trước.
  5. "The singer performed for two hours, and everyone had great fun." → Câu kết: ca sĩ biểu diễn 2 tiếng, mọi người đều vui.

--- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án A – 3250 pounds.
• Vì sao đúng: "in the end it costs me three thousand two hundred and fifty" — cụm "in the end" báo hiệu đây là giá CHỐT sau khi mặc cả.
• 3550 pounds sai: đó là giá người bán CHÀO ban đầu cho xe nhỏ ("The salesman started the small one at three thousand five hundred and fifty").
• 4250 pounds sai: đó là giá của xe TO, đã bị loại vì quá khả năng ("they want four thousand two hundred and fifty for it — more than I can manage").
👉 Mẹo: câu hỏi giá tiền luôn thả đủ 3 con số. Khoanh số đi sau "in the end / finally / we agreed on", gạch số đi sau "started at / they want / originally".

question_text: The internet makes education more accessible
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
W: You went to that open day at the university on Saturday, didn't you? How was it?
M: Impressive, on the whole. Though it's nothing like our day. Half the lectures go up on the internet the same afternoon.
W: That's the bit that thrills me. My cousin lives on a farm two hours from the nearest town, and she's halfway through a law degree from her kitchen table. Twenty years ago she simply wouldn't have had the option.
M: Same with a colleague of mine. Three kids, a full-time job, and he's doing a master's in the evenings. No moving house, and it costs a fraction of what we paid. Nobody's shut out any more.
W: It's the best thing that's happened to learning in decades.
M: Mind you, there's something you can't download. The arguments in the corridor at midnight, the drama club, the friends you make in the canteen queue. That's what those three years were about for me. Take that away and what have you got? A very expensive set of videos.
W: Hmm. I'll grant you the friendships were nice. But was that really the point? My brother kept himself to himself the whole way through, hardly went to a single party, and came out with a first and a brilliant job. Plenty of students get their degree quietly and do perfectly well.
M: You'd have felt differently if you'd lived in halls.
W: I doubt it. What does worry me, though, is the menu of courses these days. My nephew's prospectus offered over four hundred modules. He picked a bit of film, a bit of economics, a bit of Spanish, and ended up with a degree no employer understood. Sometimes less choice would do students a favour.
M: Would it? That kind of choice is how you stumble on what you're actually good at. I only discovered archaeology because I wandered into the wrong lecture in my first year. Narrow everything down and you just get identical graduates.
W: We'll have to differ on that one.
M: Then you'll hate my next idea. I'd push universities to fight each other much harder. Rank the teaching, let them chase the brightest students. Nothing raises standards like a bit of rivalry.
W: And who pays for it? My old department spent a fortune on glossy brochures and a new reception area just to climb the league tables, and it cut two tutors to do it. Rivalry made it look better and teach worse.
M: That's bad management, not rivalry.
W: Call it what you like. Students got less for their money.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. The internet makes education more accessible → Both: Nữ: "That's the bit that thrills me." (em họ ở trang trại học luật tại nhà). Nam: "Same with a colleague of mine." + "Nobody's shut out any more." Cả hai đồng ý.
2. Social interactions are essential to university life → Man: Nam: "That's what those three years were about for me. Take that away and what have you got?" Nữ bác: "But was that really the point?" + "Plenty of students get their degree quietly and do perfectly well." Bẫy: nữ "I'll grant you the friendships were nice" rồi gạt đi; "I doubt it."
3. A diverse curriculum is not always a good thing → Woman: Nữ: "Sometimes less choice would do students a favour." (cháu chọn lung tung, bằng cấp không ai hiểu). Nam bác: "Would it? That kind of choice is how you stumble on what you're actually good at." Chốt: "We'll have to differ on that one."
4. Competitions between universities should be encouraged → Man: Nam: "I'd push universities to fight each other much harder." + "Nothing raises standards like a bit of rivalry." Nữ bác: "Rivalry made it look better and teach worse." Bẫy: không có từ ‘competition’; phải hiểu ‘rivalry / fight each other / league tables’.

question_text: What does the announcer say about the new novel?
options: It is different from his earlier works
It is romantic and soft
It is less famous than his earlier works
explanation:
Good evening. Tonight I'd like to talk about the latest book from James Parker. For fifteen years he has been the name people reach for when they want a gentle story about two people falling in love, the kind of soft, romantic read you finish in a weekend. So when his publisher announced a crime novel, a few magazines predicted it would cost him his fame and most of his loyal readers.
They could not have been more wrong. Shadow in the Night is a sharp turn away from everything he has published before. There are no candlelit dinners here. Instead we get a missing witness, a town full of secrets and a detective who trusts nobody. From the opening chapter the tension never lets go, and in its first month the book outsold every one of his love stories.
So where does he go from here? It would be easy for him to stay in this darker territory now that it is selling so well, and I can understand why his long-time readers are missing the old warmth. But following the sales figures, or the loudest group of fans, is not how good writers grow. The reviews of this book were generous, but they were also honest. Several pointed out that the middle chapters drag and that two of the characters feel thin. Before he puts pen to paper again, Parker would do well to sit down with those comments and take them seriously. A writer who does that will find his own direction, whatever shelf the next book ends up on, and his readers, old and new, will follow him there.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. Đáp án: It is different from his earlier works. Bằng chứng: "Shadow in the Night is a sharp turn away from everything he has published before." Bẫy: 'romantic and soft' là mô tả các sách CŨ; 'less famous' là dự đoán của tạp chí đã sai ("They could not have been more wrong.").
2. Đáp án: He should listen to critics before writing his next work. Bằng chứng: "Before he puts pen to paper again, Parker would do well to sit down with those comments and take them seriously." Bẫy: tiếp tục thể loại mới ("stay in this darker territory") và quay lại dòng cũ ("missing the old warmth") đều bị gạt: "following the sales figures, or the loudest group of fans, is not how good writers grow."

question_text: There is too much information on the Internet
options: Man
Woman
Both
explanation:
W: How's that research project going? You were looking up something about the history of the town, weren't you?
M: It's been a nightmare, to be honest. Every time I type in a question, I get thousands of pages back. There's simply more information out there than anyone could read in ten lifetimes. Half the time I just close the laptop and give up.
W: Hmm. But a decent library has more books than you could ever get through as well, and nobody walks out of one feeling defeated. Surely the real issue is not knowing where to start?
M: Well, a library has a librarian who's already sorted everything for you. Online, nobody's done that. Which is why it takes real practice to dig out anything trustworthy: knowing which words to search for, which sites to ignore, who's actually behind a page.
W: My nephew's school runs a whole course on that now. How to spot a fake website, how to check who wrote something and when. They're learning in a few weeks what took me years to work out on my own.
M: Lucky him.
W: Actually, I've noticed something about myself lately. I used to read a novel in one sitting. Now my mind starts jumping about after a couple of pages, as if I'm looking for the next link to click. I'm convinced all those hours online have rewired the way I process things.
M: Haven't you just got busier? I'll grant you I check my phone far more than I used to, and I probably read shorter articles. But that's a habit, not a change in how my brain works. Put a good argument in front of me and I can follow it just as well as I could twenty years ago.
W: If you say so.
M: What does bother me is my daughter. If a video takes more than three seconds to load, she's already moved on to something else. She won't sit through a film without her phone in her hand.
W: Tell me about it. My students can't wait two minutes for a page to print without sighing. They expect everything instantly: answers, replies, results. Nobody has the patience to wait for anything any more.
M: Then again, we're the ones who handed them the devices in the first place.
W: True. And I'm hardly one to talk. I watch most series at double speed myself these days.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
1. There is too much information on the Internet → Man: Nam: "There's simply more information out there than anyone could read in ten lifetimes." Nữ phản bác bằng câu hỏi tu từ: "Surely the real issue is not knowing where to start?" Bẫy: nữ có nhắc thư viện cũng nhiều sách, nhưng là để bác ý của nam.
2. Finding information on the Internet requires skills → Both: Nam: "it takes real practice to dig out anything trustworthy". Nữ đồng tình qua trải nghiệm: "My nephew's school runs a whole course on that now." Không ai nói ‘skills’ nhưng cả hai cùng ý cần kỹ năng.
3. The use of the Internet affects the way we think. → Woman: Nữ: "I'm convinced all those hours online have rewired the way I process things." Nam bác: "that's a habit, not a change in how my brain works." Bẫy: nam "I'll grant you I check my phone far more than I used to" (đồng ý một phần rồi gạt đi).
4. The Internet makes young people less patient. → Both: Nam: "If a video takes more than three seconds to load, she's already moved on". Nữ: "Tell me about it." + "Nobody has the patience to wait for anything any more." Cả hai đồng ý.

question_text: Four people are talking about doing exercise. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: My wife assumes I took up cycling to get rid of my belly, but that was never the reason, and the bathroom scales don't interest me much. It started last winter, when I kept nodding off in the three o'clock meeting. So now I ride for half an hour before I get to the office, and the difference is remarkable. I clear my emails in half the usual time, I'm sharper with clients, and last month my manager asked me to lead a new project. That's what gets me on the bike on cold mornings.
Speaker B: People sometimes think I must hate sport because I complain about it so much, but that's not true at all. I quite like the idea of it, and I go to an aerobics class twice a week because I know it's good for me. The problem is what happens to my body. Ten minutes in, my legs feel like lead and I can barely catch my breath. By the end I'm dragging myself to the changing room, and then I need a long sit-down and an early night. Everyone promises it gets easier. Two years on, I'm still waiting.
Speaker C: I'm not a sporty person by nature, and I've never been very competitive. I did try going to the gym on my own for a while, with my headphones in, but I got bored and gave up after a month. These days it's five-a-side football on Thursdays with the lads from my street, and badminton with my cousins at the weekend. Honestly, we're all pretty hopeless. We spend more time laughing at missed shots than scoring, and the best bit is the drink afterwards, when we tease whoever played worst. I wouldn't miss it.
Speaker D: My colleagues keep telling me a lunchtime workout would make me sharper in the afternoons, and my brother drags me along to his badminton club now and then. I go to keep the peace, but I spend the whole hour watching the clock. And it isn't that it wears me out, because it doesn't. Honestly, I just can't stand any of it: the sweat, the noise, the smelly changing rooms, people shouting instructions at me. I don't see the point, and I never have. Give me a good book and a comfortable chair any day.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
ĐÁP ÁN:
- Improve work performance → Speaker A: "I clear my emails in half the usual time, I'm sharper with clients, and last month my manager asked me to lead a new project".
- Hate exercising → Speaker D: "I just can't stand any of it".
- Find exercise tiring → Speaker B: "Ten minutes in, my legs feel like lead and I can barely catch my breath".
- Have fun exercising with others → Speaker C: "We spend more time laughing at missed shots than scoring".
BẪY:
- Speaker A nhắc tới "Exercise to lose weight": "My wife assumes I took up cycling to get rid of my belly, but that was never the reason, and the bathroom scales don't interest me much." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của A.
- Speaker B nhắc tới "Hate exercising": "People sometimes think I must hate sport because I complain about it so much, but that's not true at all." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của B.
- Speaker C nhắc tới "Enjoy exercising alone": "I did try going to the gym on my own for a while, with my headphones in, but I got bored and gave up after a month." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của C.
- Speaker D nhắc tới "Improve work performance / Have fun exercising with others": "My colleagues keep telling me a lunchtime workout would make me sharper in the afternoons, and my brother drags me along to his badminton club now and then." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của D.
PHƯƠNG ÁN THỪA: "Enjoy exercising alone" (bị nhắc làm bẫy ở Speaker C); "Exercise to lose weight" (bị nhắc làm bẫy ở Speaker A) → không ai chọn.

question_text: Four people are talking about protecting the environment. Match each person to the correct information.
explanation:
Speaker A: Everyone on my road is very proud of their recycling boxes, and fair enough, but rinsing out plastic bottles has never been my thing. What I'm strict about is the switch on the wall. If a room's empty, the lights go off, full stop. The washing machine only goes on when it's completely full, and I unplug the telly and all the chargers before bed. My kids roll their eyes at me, but our bills have nearly halved since last winter, and I like to think the power station has an easier time thanks to our family.
Speaker B: My neighbour cycles to the office every day and keeps trying to get me on a bike, but the hills round here are far too steep for me, so that idea didn't last. Last spring I made a different decision: the car stays in the garage from Monday to Friday. I catch the number forty-two at the end of my road instead. It adds fifteen minutes each way, but I read on the top deck, so I don't really mind. One fewer car in the morning jam, that's my small contribution, and I arrive at my desk far calmer too.
Speaker C: People expect me to say I've given up the car, but I can't, honestly. I live miles from the nearest station. What I do instead will probably sound lazy. Almost everything I buy, I order from my laptop on the sofa. One delivery van going down my street replaces dozens of separate trips to the retail park, dozens of engines circling for a parking space. I put everything into one weekly order so it all comes in a single box. My neighbour laughs at me, but I reckon my armchair habit is greener than her Saturday drive into town.
Speaker D: My husband's the one who goes round switching off lights and unplugging things. That's his department, not mine. Mine is the tap. I've got a timer in the shower, four minutes and out. I rinse vegetables in a bowl, and then that bowl goes straight onto the garden. The day I read how many litres a dripping tap wastes in a year, I got the toolbox out and fixed ours myself. My children say I'm strict about it, and I am. It's the thing we'll run short of first, so every drop I keep matters.

--- GIẢI THÍCH ĐÁP ÁN ---
ĐÁP ÁN:
- protects the environment by not driving to work. → Speaker B: "the car stays in the garage from Monday to Friday. I catch the number forty-two at the end of my road instead".
- protects the environment by shopping online. → Speaker C: "Almost everything I buy, I order from my laptop on the sofa".
- protects the environment by using less water. → Speaker D: "I've got a timer in the shower, four minutes and out".
- protects the environment by using less electricity. → Speaker A: "If a room's empty, the lights go off, full stop".
BẪY:
- Speaker A nhắc tới "protects the environment by recycling plastic bottles.": "Everyone on my road is very proud of their recycling boxes, and fair enough, but rinsing out plastic bottles has never been my thing." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của A.
- Speaker B nhắc tới "protects the environment by cycling to work.": "My neighbour cycles to the office every day and keeps trying to get me on a bike, but the hills round here are far too steep for me, so that idea didn't last." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của B.
- Speaker C nhắc tới "protects the environment by not driving to work.": "People expect me to say I've given up the car, but I can't, honestly." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của C.
- Speaker D nhắc tới "protects the environment by using less electricity.": "My husband's the one who goes round switching off lights and unplugging things." → gạt đi, không phải đáp án của D.
PHƯƠNG ÁN THỪA: "protects the environment by cycling to work." (bị nhắc làm bẫy ở Speaker B); "protects the environment by recycling plastic bottles." (bị nhắc làm bẫy ở Speaker A) → không ai chọn.

Good morning, I'm calling about flights to Edinburgh next Tuesday. Yes, I saw three prices online and got confused. The evening flight is four hundred pounds, which is too much for me. --- GIẢI THÍCH: Đáp án B – 350 pounds.
• Vì sao đúng: "So the morning flight it is — three hundred and fifty pounds, you said? Perfect, let's book that one" — chuyến sáng đúng 350 và đã đặt.
